slides.title: What is an / [embedding]?
slides.hook: "How do I get my money back?" shares no word with the refund doc. BM25 scored it 0; an embedding, which turns text into a point, ranked it 1st of 5.
inside: Sparse keyword vectors next to dense ones
Four questions with no content word in common
Why near only counts inside one model

slides.title: Text becomes / [numbers]
slides.text: An embedding model turns text into a fixed-length list of floats. Here, spaCy's `en_core_web_md`: 300 numbers.
bullets: OpenAI's embeddings guide: "An embedding is a vector (list) of floating point numbers."
One number alone means little. Meaning sits in where the whole point lands.

slides.title: Every text gets / [300] numbers
slides.text: A word, a sentence and 5 joined docs all come out at 300 numbers, so any two texts from this model can be compared.
bullets: all-MiniLM-L6-v2: 384 dimensions; input past 256 word pieces is truncated (model card).

slides.title: Sparse vs / [dense] vectors
slides.text: A keyword vector has one slot per word in the vocabulary, and most slots are 0. A dense vector puts signal in every slot.

visuals.caption: "How do I get my money back?"

options.note: None of its words is in the 5 docs' vocabulary

slides.after: The keyword vector is all zeros, so its score against every doc is 0.

slides.title: Keywords find / [no] match
slides.text: 5 made-up help-centre docs. BM25, a keyword ranker, scores the refund question against each one:

visuals.label: Query: "How do I get my money back?"

chunks.text: Refunds are issued to the original card within 5 business days.
Invoices are emailed on the first day of each month.

slides.after: All 5 docs score 0.0: the question shares no word with any of them.

slides.title: Close in / [meaning]
slides.text: Embed the same question and score it against the 5 docs by cosine similarity (1.0 means the same direction):

visuals.caption: "How do I get my money back?"

options.output: Refunds are issued to the original card within 5 business days.
Invoices are emailed on the first day of each month.
Add team members from the Seats page.
Export your data as a CSV file … / Reset your password …

slides.after: Of the refund doc's words, "business", "refunds" and "card" sit closest to "money".

slides.title: Search is / [nearest] points
slides.text: Once meaning is geometry, semantic search is a nearest-neighbour lookup:

steps: Store the vectors with their text.
Embed the question with the same model.
Score the question against the stored vectors.

slides.after: Step 3 has to use the model from step 1.

slides.title: Four questions, / no shared [content] words
slides.text: None of these questions shares a content word with its answer. Each one's nearest doc, by cosine:

options.setting: "How do I get my money back?"
"Can I download everything as a spreadsheet?"

slides.after: BM25 finds Export for the spreadsheet question through "as" and "a", and only Export for the colleague question, through "a". Read cosine scores as a ranking within one model.

slides.title: Close can / be [wrong]
slides.text: Averaging drops word order, and this setup also skips stop words. Two pairs with opposite meanings:

options.output: "Monthly plans can be refunded." and "Monthly plans cannot be refunded."
options.note: "can" and "not" are stop words, so the vectors match

options.output: "The customer refunds the company." and "The company refunds the customer."

slides.after: Test negation and word order on your own model before you trust its nearest hits.

slides.title: Don't mix / [models]
slides.text: Distances only mean something between vectors from the same model. A small test: questions from `en_core_web_md`, docs from `en_core_web_lg`.
slides.after: md is a pruned copy of lg's vectors ("refund" is identical in both), and mixing them still moved an answer. Re-embed everything when you change models.

slides.title: Embeddings: / when to [use]

cards.title: Use them when
items: Users ask in their own words
Synonyms and paraphrases miss in keyword search
You can embed docs and queries with one model

cards.title: Add keywords when
items: Queries carry IDs, codes or exact names
A negation like "cannot" has to count (test yours first)
You need to explain why a doc matched

slides.after: For word order, a reranker that reads query and doc together can help.

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: Embedding: text becomes a fixed-length list of floats
Similar meaning lands close in the embedding space
Dense vectors can match words a query didn't use
Compare scores within one model as a ranking
Embed queries and docs with the same model
Test negation and word order on your model

slides.line: Search means finding the nearest points. Next: what near means, and what cosine, dot product and L2 each reward.
